chapters.html:
On Mydei’s last day as a man, he decides to take a bath.

Bathing has never been something he has particularly enjoyed. As embarrassing as it is to admit—even to himself—the mere sight of pools of water has always made his chest feel far too tight. It doesn’t matter that the baths of Okhema are a far cry from the frigid waves of the Sea of Souls—his foolish body has never quite gotten the memo.

But a Kremnoan must face their weaknesses head-on—and this rule surely holds double for a Kremnoan destined to brandish the power of Strife in their own two hands.

Regardless, the truth remains; once Mydei manages to squash that squirming thing in his chest, the sensation of bathing is nice enough. Besides, he can hardly wander through the picturesque streets of Okhema in his current state. Wandering around coated in the dust and grime of battle will draw questions he doesn’t have the time or patience for.

So. A bath it is.

It’s going well enough; a few repetitions of a breathing exercise recommended by the Ladies Tribios has his mind pleasantly blank. Enough to focus on the sensations, at least. The water is a fair bit too cold—but the steam still fills his lungs pleasantly, making golden hair cling to the sides of his face. And then—

“Mydeimos! Mydei!”

Mydei squints one eye open. The steam from the baths conceals much of the figure before him, but the voice is unmistakable. Indeed—it would be hard for anyone in Okhema to confuse Phainon’s voice with anyone else’s.

A small, traitorous part of him is thrilled—bathing is so much easier with Phainon around. As ceaselessly frustrating as the man is, he is remarkably good at keeping Mydei’s mind busy enough for that cowardly thing inside him to forget that they’re submerged in water. Phainon’s presence gives his body something else entirely to focus on—and, sure enough, the tightness in his chest is replaced with a fluttering in his stomach. It’s not a new development by any means—but it never ceases to be frustrating.

“What do you want,” he says dryly.

“So prickly, Mydeimos!” Phainon huffs. “I just wanted to congratulate you on your ascension—I know the perils of Nikador’s trial better than anyone.”

Something like guilt—or perhaps shame—flickers in Phainon’s eyes. Mydei ignores it. Warriors do not dwell on such emotions, and he certainly isn’t going to give Phainon the implicit permission to linger on them by acknowledging them. And… well, perhaps his silence is payback for the way that he never pointed out the cracks in Mydei’s armor over the past few weeks.

Phainon has truly been in rare form lately. Buying Mydei street food after their spars; dragging him to the baths for a stolen moment of relaxation; sitting in considerate silence when Mydei has shared some story from his past. Mydei has even heard him defending Mydei’s honor to a few gossiping Kremnoan soldiers—something that should have humiliated him. Mydei is their commander; he ought to deal with such a thing. But Phainon—unaware of Mydei’s presence just around the corner—swooped in without a second thought. And the last time they were in bed—

Mydei shakes himself slightly—that was enough of that. How could he hope to be the next Lance of Fury with such a wandering mind?

When he turns his attention back to Phainon, though, he’s immediately reminded why he zoned out in the first place. The man’s jabbering on uselessly—something about a dromas and an overturned cart.

“Get to the point,” he interrupts.

Phainon chuckles. “As acerbic as ever, Mydei,” he says, jabbing him with his elbow. “Anyway! I was just saying—it’s a pleasure to stand before the esteemednew Lance of Fury,” he winks. “What is it they're calling you now? The 'Roaring Lion of Castrum Kremnos?' The 'Kremnoan Dawnbringer'?" Then, more consideringly: "I don't really blame them, though. You were amazing earlier. You definitely came in the nick of time."

Mydei rolls his eyes, even as his faithless heart can’t help but flutter.“Call me that again and I’ll grind you into dust, haikas. You know well I have no use for such inane titles and feckless flattery.”

“Don’t like it?” Phainon pouts. “Fine. Congratulations rescinded. Though it wouldn’t kill you to accept some praise for once, Mydei.”

“It’s called humility, Deliverer. Perhaps you would benefit from practicing it,” Mydei shoots back.

Phainon laughs at that—a proper laugh, not those fake little things he supplies to the throngs of Okhemans who worship him like a Titan come to life.

“Maybe so,” he grins.

The little flicker of pride Mydei feels at causing such a laugh in Phainon is immediately overshadowed as it fades into a smile.

Phainon’s usual smile is bright—as bright as a beam of sunlight, and just as blinding. It’s a smile that sends the hearts of all Okhemans alike aflutter. Mydei nearly pities them—they don’t know the true mischief that lies behind the eyes of their beloved Deliverer.

Mischief that—as of now—is glaringly absent. Phainon looks much more… subdued. This smile is still bright—enough to daze anyone foolish enough to get too close. Mydei doubts most people would be able to tell the difference. But anyone who knows Phainon well could point out how forced it is in an instant. It doesn’t even reach his eyes. His pitiful attempts at getting a rise out of Mydei are obviously lacking as well.

It’s a bit insulting that Phainon thinks Mydei would buy such an obvious farce. Mydei and Phainon are not friends, necessarily. Not in the way that Castorice and Hyacine are, for example. There’s no effusive praise or enthusiastic greetings. Besides—as a rule, Kremnoans don’t have friends in the way that Okhemans do. They have allies. And that—well. Mydei is certainly confident calling Phainon an ally.

Phainon may be bumbling sometimes and infuriating always, but he is, without a doubt, an ally. Mydei’s closest, even.

Phainon certainly knows Mydei well, too. Not only his mind, but his body as well. Their frequent trysts have seen to that.

Nikador’s Fury, what is wrong with Mydei today?

At the very least, it’s clear that Mydei isn’t the only one with a wandering mind. When Mydei reaches for a goblet of wine, Phainon’s gaze drags along his muscles like a caress. Phainon clears his throat a second later—but the flush on his pale skin remains.

“I also wanted to say goodbye,” Phainon continues, shattering the momentary silence. “I… heard you’ll be returning to Castrum Kremnos at action hour. To continue the fight against the Black Tide.

“That’s correct,” Mydei acknowledges, tipping his head.

Silence stretches between them for a moment too long—and then Phainon clears his throat.

“So,” he says—almost hesitant—“before you go, I was wondering if you would be willing to talk in private. In my chambers, perhaps?”

Mydei does his best to ignore the frantic beating of his traitorous heart. He’s tried his best not to think about what his imminent departure means for himself and Phainon—but face-to-face like this, Titans, it’s so much harder.

He should say no. It’s hard enough to remind himself that their trysts don’t mean anything—can’t mean anything, no matter how much his heart protests—on a good day. It’s just stress relief. A way to burn off steam. It’s a lie they both cling to—which is why they only ever tug the other into bed after a battle or an argument. They never even speak about it—they just drift from tackling to fucking. They have never once proposed a tryst like this. Mydei isn’t stupid, though. He knows what Phainon’s asking.

All at once, Mydei’s resolve melts away.

He sighs. Rolls his eyes. Sets his glass down with a clink of metal on marble. “What do you think, Deliverer?”

Mydei doesn’t think he’ll ever tire of the silly little smile Phainon gets when he walks Mydei back to his room. It’s a hesitant thing—like he fears Mydei will change his mind any moment. It’s an illogical fear—Mydei never has before, and he certainly isn’t going to now.

One more time can’t hurt anything, he tells himself. And chances are that it really is going to be the last time—Mydei is under no illusions about the risks of the Flamechase Journey. Especially not now.

He knows Phainon isn’t either—he’s not stupid. Though you wouldn’t know it from the way he’s practically bouncing from foot to foot, brushing their fingers together with an expression more befitting a child with a handful of stolen figs rather than a warrior about to have sex with the same man he’s been sleeping with for months.

“I’m happy to help,” Phainon says smoothly.

“Of course you were,” Megaira forces out a giggle—an attempt at demureness, surely. Mydei’s skin crawls—with second-hand embarrassment, he convinces himself. “Well, I’d love to repay you. Perhaps… I could take you out for dinner? Are you free tonight?”

End Notes

Thanks so much for reading!! Please leave a comment if you’d like to make me squeal and run around my room like a feral cat o7

I also maaaybe have plans for a sequel that’ll be less sad. Wink wink. So if you're interested in that, let me know!

Notes for nerds:

1.) Megaira - one of the Erinnyes (furies); her name translates to “grudge” or “jealousy”; I thought it would be funny and very on-the-nose. Fun fact: Megara is also the wife of Heracles.

2.) Hyacinth - Hey ao3 user k1tschii, why’d you reference Hyacine’s flower? GOOD QUESTION. I associate Phainon with Apollon; both are associated with sunlight, truth, prophecy, and “deliverance” (in Apollon’s case, primarily from illness). Hyacinthos was said to be a young Spartan man that Apollon fell in love with—and accidentally killed. Whoops. Does that perhaps remind you of anyone else you know? I didn’t go too crazy with this because I figured Mydei wouldn’t be too prone to flowery language. But I had to throw it in there because this comparison makes me crazy.

3.) Kline - a sort of bed-couch ancient Greeks reclined & slept on.

Oh boy now we’re getting into language territory. My apologies in advance; I’m what we in the business call ~linguistically challenged~. I chose to use modern Greek because I was a liiittle too lazy to research authentic ancient Greek terms of endearment, LOL.

4.) Chryse mou - to my understanding, it’s the masculine form of “golden one”

5.) Agapi mou - my love

6.) Kykeon - a favorite drink of Greek peasants that is often associated with the Eleusinian Mysteries. (That is, a secretive religious rite focusing on Demeter & Persephone.) I chose to have it be drunk in Aedes Elysiae due to the likelihood of its population being made up of poor farmers, and because of its visual association with wheat & the harvest. I realize that Demeter would probably be more closely associated with Georios, but shhh.
